tour.title: Active RF Forecast Path
tour.description: Start with the implemented public scorer: the Random Forest surrogate, training entry point, daily inference, and the support utilities that convert weather/terrain/snowpack signals into risk outputs.
tour.languageLesson: In this repo the active public ML path is a Python/sklearn-style batch scorer, not an online deep-learning service.

tour.title: Feature Engineering and Physical Proxies
tour.description: Review terrain, runout, snowpack proxy, avalanche-prone terrain, regions, and forecast bulletin helpers to understand what evidence feeds the RF model and the public grid.
tour.languageLesson: Several model inputs are engineered proxies; treat them as decision-support features unless backed by local measured evidence.

tour.title: Publication and Claim Controls
tour.description: Follow the path from inference to public eligibility, model-status state, forecast publication, and release gates. This is where prediction outputs are separated from publishable claims.
tour.languageLesson: The repo uses explicit publication and release guardrails so model output does not automatically become an operational claim.

tour.title: MTS-LSTM Candidate Lane
tour.description: Inspect the sequence-model code and loaders. This lane is implemented enough to test/model sequence candidates, but it is separate from the active public RF scorer.
tour.languageLesson: Sequence models need stricter temporal split discipline than tabular RF baselines; do not compare them without matching leakage controls.

tour.title: SAR Shadow Segmentation Lane
tour.description: Review U-Net/SwinUNet segmentation, SAR training/evaluation, SnowSlide diagnostics, and acceptance policy. This is the remote-sensing lane and remains shadow-gated.
tour.languageLesson: Segmentation acceptance is controlled by heldout precision/recall/F1/FPR gates, not by visual plausibility alone.

tour.title: Swiss RAvaFcast Reproduction
tour.description: Inspect the research-only reproduction lane: feature audits, RF4 training, calibration/evaluation, GPxyz interpolation, aggregation, and manifest discipline.
tour.languageLesson: Swiss reproduction artifacts are evidence for method discipline; they are not direct proof of Himalayan accuracy.

tour.title: Himalayan Partner Evidence Gate
tour.description: Open the Himalayan contract and triage scripts to see how partner evidence, D_tidy-grade labels, station metadata, source manifests, and holdout rows are validated before any local accuracy claim.
tour.languageLesson: The Himalayan lane starts with evidence contracts and source governance, not model promotion.

tour.title: Remote Compute and Test Gates
tour.description: Finish with Modal orchestration, trigger/poll scripts, backend tests, and CI workflows that bound heavy training/evaluation and verify release safety.
tour.languageLesson: Heavy compute is orchestrated and gated; local graph inspection should not be mistaken for a fresh training run.
